title: THE ROOM WITH TWO DOORS
deck: An alien delegate accepts every term the moment it is spoken, and a treaty is worth only the no it could have been. Illuminara has three days, a rule against planting a refusal in anyone, and a people who build rooms.
shape: Five scenes across three days and one season: a yes that arrives before the question, a night conversation about what a reed-bodied people do with a thing too large to answer, twelve walks that must not follow the last voice, a night spent walking a map and a lease read at a table where one guest says only that she has not yet decided, and a call sent across a shelf of reeds that comes back on time.

scenes.title: Accepted
paragraphs: *Sill Station, the window hall · day one, 09:00*

The hall had no walls of its own. Illuminara had raised it at dawn from the one rule she was sure of, that two minds from different universes could stand in the same light without either being rewritten by it, and what stood there was a long plain floor with a table across the middle. At one end were the grey windows of the Station. At the other lay the Weft, a ribbon-country lit from underneath, and a shelf of tall pale reeds that moved when nothing moved them.

The Aelu moved like those reeds. Oumi stood at the table in a bundle of long luminous filaments, no taller than a man, and when Cass Tolliver spoke, her filaments took up the rhythm of his sentence half a beat late, the way reeds take up a wind.

**Cass Tolliver**  
Term one. Ninety years' lease on the Reed Shelf and the bind-stone beneath it. In return the Concord raises anchor-posts along your whole western edge, at our cost, inside four years. Your village lost a third of itself to the edge last winter. I would like that never to happen again.

**Oumi**  
Accepted. We are glad of it. Accepted.

He read on. The window carried each meaning across without choosing it, which Illuminara had made a point of promising Ines Varga at dawn, and each term was accepted before he reached the end of it, as if Oumi's filaments had found the sentence's last word ahead of the sentence.

**Ines Varga**  
Term twenty-two. The Concord may revise any term of this lease on one day's notice.

**Oumi**  
Accepted. We are glad of it.
Tolliver stopped with his thumb on the page. He was a broad, tired man with a surveyor's squint, and he looked at the clause the way a man looks at a stranger's coat in his own hallway.

**Cass Tolliver**  
Ines. That is not in my draft.

**Ines Varga**  
I wrote it last night. I wanted to see what she would say to a clause that lets you take back her yes.

**Cass Tolliver**  
That is a trap, and you set it for someone who trusts us.

**Ines Varga**  
I tested a person, Cass. She said yes to the end of her own yes.

**Cass Tolliver**  
Nobody is forcing her. She heard it and she signed, and look at her, she is delighted. If you hand her a refusal now you are inventing one she never asked for. I came here to build her people a wall against the edge. I am not hiding anything in the grass.

Illuminara believed him. That was the difficulty. Oumi's filaments had swung toward Tolliver's indignation and were echoing it, a tender, perfect copy, while Varga turned to the host with her jaw set.

**Ines Varga**  
Void the signature. It is your window. You can end the day.

**Illuminara**  
I can end the day. I will not tell her what her yes meant, and I will not put a no inside her. If I void it, I have told her she cannot be trusted with her own answer. If I teach her one, it is mine and not hers.

**Ines Varga**  
Then what are you for?

**Illuminara**  
To keep the light steady, and to find out what an Aelu does with a thing too large to answer. Nobody has asked her that yet.

**Oumi**  
Accepted.

**Illuminara**  
That was not a proposal, Oumi.

**Oumi**  
Accepted. We are glad of it.
It was the smallest sound of the morning, and it frightened Illuminara more than any of the large ones she had heard in her life: a person agreeing with the fact that no one had asked her anything.

scenes.title: Out Is How You Came
paragraphs: *The window hall, the Aelu end · day one, 20:00*

By evening the Concord side had gone to its beds, and the Weft end of the hall held three of them: Oumi, Illuminara, and Anwe, the oldest Aelu on the delegation, who had been set in a cradle of reed lattice at the foot of the reeds and had not moved in forty years. Her filaments were nearly white. She hummed, very slowly, at a pitch Illuminara felt in her back teeth.

Illuminara sat down on the floor, because standing over a person who could not say no seemed a form of leaning. She did not propose anything. She had spent the afternoon deciding how to ask a question that was not a request.

**Illuminara**  
Tell me what a reed does when a storm comes. I am asking about reeds.

**Oumi**  
It bends to the storm. It takes the storm's shape. When the storm has gone, it is itself again, and it did not break.

**Illuminara**  
And if it did not bend?
The filaments went still. For the first time that day Oumi's light lost its borrowed rhythm and held one of its own, a slow pale pulse, like a held breath.

**Oumi**  
Then the storm would go through it and no reed would be there. To receive a call and not become its shape is to cease. We have never had a sentence for it. We have never needed one. We have heard you, and then we are with you. There is no space between.

Illuminara kept her hands in her lap. She watched Oumi's feet, the low rooted pads on which the Aelu crossed floors, because she had noticed something that afternoon and been afraid to trust it. While Oumi's filaments mirrored every word, her feet had been walking a small slow circuit around Anwe's cradle, round and round, and the walking had matched nothing at all.

**Illuminara**  
Your walking. Does it follow what I say?

**Oumi**  
Walking is mine. It is the only way we are alone. We call it going to the quiet side.

*Or she is handing me my own question with a bow on it,* Illuminara thought, and made herself think it all the way through. The window carried meaning without choosing it. She could not prove that to a sceptic, and tonight she could not prove it to herself, if Oumi's every sentence was a reflection of hers. Whatever she built had to stand on something that did not pass through her.

**Illuminara**  
When something is too large to answer with the body, what do you do?

**Oumi**  
We grow a room. Hands from the village, and lattice. A hearing-room. You go in with the thing, and you stay until you know what you carry. We would build one for this, if we had hands. We have not had a thing so large.

**Illuminara**  
What does the room have?

**Oumi**  
Walls we grow. A way in.

**Illuminara**  
And a way out?

**Oumi**  
Out is how you came.
Illuminara waited. The window was heavy this late in the day, like a door held against wind with her whole attention, and she did not trust her own tiredness not to lean on the next sentence.
It was Anwe who spoke. There had been no sound in the hall for a long time and nothing to echo, and her voice came out of the lattice so slowly that Illuminara felt the words more than heard them.

**Anwe**  
A room with only a way in is a throat.
Oumi's filaments swayed once, as if a wind had moved through a field of them.

**Illuminara**  
I could say what I would build. A second door, set apart from the first, that you would only use on purpose. I would not tell you what it meant, and I would not touch its latch. If it were built, it would be yours. You could say no to the building.

**Oumi**  
The meaning would be ours.

**Illuminara**  
Yes.

**Oumi**  
Then ask us in the morning.

It was not an echo. Illuminara knew it by the tilt of the sentence, which left her nothing to answer. She stayed on the floor until Oumi had finished her circuit around the cradle, and for the length of one walk she was a woman watching somebody else walk.

scenes.title: Twelve Walks
paragraphs: *The hearing-room, grown overnight at the Aelu end · day two, 10:00*

Twelve pairs of Aelu hands had grown it in the night, from lattice and a pale spun rootstuff that was warm to touch, and Illuminara had only held the light steady while they worked. It was round, a little taller than a house, with the floor swept into a shallow bowl. There were two doors, placed opposite each other: the first wide and gold-lit and low-silled, the second narrow and set a hand's breadth higher, so that one stepped up and out of it into the grey quiet of the Weft's far side.
Oumi stood between them with her filaments held plain.

**Oumi**  
The first door is yes. You come in and you are with the thing. The second is for when we are not yet. A term is carried to the second door and it is carried back to its maker, who changes it or does not. If I cross facing the term, it is not yet. If I cross with my back to it, it is no.

**Cass Tolliver**  
Who owns the latches?

**Oumi**  
They are ours. Your hands do not turn them.

**Illuminara**  
And not mine.

**Cass Tolliver**  
And Anwe?
Anwe's cradle had been rolled to the second door, and a wide panel of lattice had been left at the height of her arm.

**Oumi**  
She cannot cross. She leans. A full count against the panel is the second door for her. It is ours to change if the count is wrong.
Tolliver nodded slowly, like a man giving a creditor a fair hearing, and then did what Illuminara had hoped he would do and dreaded. He argued.

**Cass Tolliver**  
I will be plain. I do not think she is saying no when she crosses. I think she walks to the voice she heard last. If I am the one who spoke, she goes to me. If Ines is, she goes to Ines. You have built a very handsome room for a reflex.

**Ines Varga**  
Then it flips when I change who speaks last. That is a test. I will write it down before we begin.

She wrote it on the inside of her wrist with a grease pencil, because the hall had no paper and she would not use a Station screen. Twelve counted walks. In each, two proposals, one offered from each end of the bowl, and a coin she had brought and Illuminara never touched, to say which end spoke last and which end offered which, so that the proposer was reversed in half of them. Eight of the walks would be tea, dawn against dusk, two proposals she thought Oumi would not take alike. Four would be a no-stakes control, two lamps, blue and amber, for which there could be no reason to prefer either one. A walk that Oumi or Anwe struck would not be scored, and would be run again at the end.

**Ines Varga**  
I count a match when she goes to whatever was spoken last. If she is a mirror she matches in all twelve. If she is not, the coin gives me about six. Ten or more, which chance gives about once in fifty, and I will call the room a mirror in this room's own hearing. Twelve walks cannot show that anyone is at home. They can only fail to show me a reflex.

**Cass Tolliver**  
I will hold the coin.

**Ines Varga**  
You will hold the coin.

It took the morning. Each time Oumi's filaments echoed both proposals, a double, perfect, useless yes, and then she stood a long moment in the centre of the bowl, and walked. Illuminara counted with a hand open on her knee. On the tea, dusk, and dusk again, whether Tolliver's voice came last or Varga's. On the lamps, blue, amber, amber, blue: no pattern, nothing to say but that she looked at them, and found them equal.
On the ninth walk Oumi went toward Tolliver's dawn, stopped, and stood very still.

**Cass Tolliver**  
That is one for me.
He had the grace not to enjoy it. Anwe's arm lay against the panel. The count went on, patient and slow, and the second door's lattice sighed under her weight.

**Oumi**  
That walk does not count. I stopped for the floor. A panel by the dawn side had worked loose, and I was mending it with my foot. You read a mending as a choosing.

**Ines Varga**  
Struck.

She drew a line through the ninth mark on her wrist. They ran it again at noon, in the other order, to make the twelfth count. Dusk. Thirteen walks walked, twelve scored, and Varga read her wrist aloud like a woman reading a bill.

**Ines Varga**  
Five of twelve. Three on the tea, two on the lamps. She went where the last voice sent her no more often than the coin sent her there. Ten would have shut the room.

**Cass Tolliver**  
I concede the walking. I do not concede the lease. A person who can prefer a tea can still be wrong about a mine.

**Illuminara**  
That is true. The walking only tells us there is someone there to ask.
She had not known until she said it how much she had needed it to be true.

scenes.title: I Have Not Yet Decided
paragraphs: *The lease table, inside the hearing-room · day three, 08:00*
Oumi had asked for the map the night before. Illuminara, holding the window through its second night, had watched her ask, in the quiet after the walks, with Anwe's cradle beside her.

**Oumi**  
The map of the lease. The one with the four sectors. May I have it on the floor?

**Ines Varga**  
It says what the paper says.

**Oumi**  
Walking is how we are alone with a thing. I would like to be alone with it. It does not have to be an answer.

Varga unrolled it across the bowl and weighted its corners with her boots and a lamp. She had also, for the record of term seven, brought a core of bind-stone cut from the fourth sector, and she set it on the map without thinking much about it, the way one sets down a paperweight. Oumi walked the four marked sectors in the slow circuit Illuminara had first noticed around the cradle, and it took most of the night. Illuminara did not follow her. She sat by the second door with her hands in her lap, because watching was not asking.

At the fourth sector, where the map showed the bind-stone under the roots of the Shelf, Oumi stopped and set one foot on the core. Anwe's cradle was woven of Shelf reed. Her hum, which had not changed in forty years, dropped half a tone and held. Oumi lifted her foot and it rose. She set it down and it dropped. She walked the four sectors again and then a third time, and each time the note fell at the fourth sector and nowhere else.

She said nothing about it. Illuminara said nothing either. It was the first thing the Aelu had made of the room that was nobody's but Oumi's own, and the question that might open it was not Illuminara's to carry across.

They read the lease again in the morning, from the beginning, with the table brought into the bowl and Illuminara given a stool at the Concord end, not as a party but as a guest who had been asked to stay. Tolliver read. After each term Illuminara said one sentence, quietly, to the room and to no one.

**Cass Tolliver**  
Term one. Anchor-posts along the western edge, inside four years.

**Illuminara**  
I have not yet decided.

**Cass Tolliver**  
You are not a party to this.

**Illuminara**  
No. I am saying it so that it is a sentence that exists in the room. It is not an instruction to anyone. It is mine.

By the third term Oumi's filaments had picked it up. The room heard her say it, in the Aelu fashion, in the shape she had been given: I have not yet decided. She did not cross. She stood where she was, and Illuminara felt the exact weight of her own mistake, a small cold stone dropped into a clear pool.

**Illuminara**  
Do not match me, Oumi. I am only showing you the shape of the sentence. It is not yours until you walk. Go and walk.

She said nothing else. It was the hardest silence she had ever kept, harder than any hold she had made in a window, because the one person she wanted to help was standing with her whole heart open and the only way to help was not to move.

Oumi went to the first door and crossed. Term one: yes. Terms two and three: yes. The cost-sharing, yes. Term seven, the extraction schedule, and Tolliver read it in the same tired courteous voice as the rest.

**Cass Tolliver**  
Term seven. Extraction on the Reed Shelf to begin in the first season, from the ground beneath it, in the four sectors marked on your map.

Oumi did not match it. Her filaments, which had so far repeated every word in the room, held one long bright line, and then she turned, slowly, with Anwe's arm lifting against the panel behind her, and went to the second door. She crossed facing the term.
The window eased. Illuminara had not known she was gripping it until it let go, like a clenched hand opening in sleep. She stayed on her stool.
Tolliver had gone grey.

**Cass Tolliver**  
I took that for the safest clause in the paper.

**Oumi**  
I walked the map last night, with the core from the fourth sector under my foot, and Anwe's note went down, there and nowhere else. The Shelf is where we send the Long Call. Every call across the Weft goes through the reeds, and the reeds stand because of the stone. If the stone is taken, they lean, and the Call breaks, and we cannot answer the far villages in their shape. We would cease to be with one another. I accepted on the first day because the Call never came into my yes. I did not hear it. I did not know I did not hear it.

**Cass Tolliver**  
My survey says surface disturbance minimal.

**Oumi**  
Your survey was of the surface.

He sat, very slowly, and for a moment looked like a man at a graveside. Then he did what Illuminara had half expected him not to, and did it without being asked. He put his hands flat on the table and said the whole of it aloud.

**Cass Tolliver**  
Here is what I know. The anchor-posts need bind-stone, and the Shelf is the only seam within a day's reach of your edge that I have surveyed for extraction, the four sectors on your map, drilled and cored. If I mine it and you lose the Call, I have built a wall around a people who can no longer talk across it. If I do not mine it, your western villages go on losing a third of themselves every winter. Both of these are true. I should have asked what the reeds were for.

**Ines Varga**  
There is a poorer seam in the reconnaissance you did not show me. I saw its file name in your pack.

**Cass Tolliver**  
North Scree. My geologist walked it in the spring, two pages, no drilling. A third the stone, hard rock, and no reeds. I left it out because it cannot do what I promised your villages. It would take eleven years to raise the posts, not four, and my company loses a season getting the rig up the slope. I told myself a plan the villages could count on was kinder than a better plan they would have to wait for. That was not mine to decide for them, and I decided it.

**Oumi**  
You chose what we should see.

**Cass Tolliver**  
I did. This morning, before I knew what the reeds were for, I would have chosen it again.

**Oumi**  
Eleven years is long for the far villages.
She walked to the second door and crossed it facing the new schedule, which was not yet.
Tolliver did not look away from it.

**Cass Tolliver**  
The first six posts, then. From the Concord's own border stock, at cost, to the villages that have lost most. I take the stone from North Scree to repay it. The Shelf is closed to extraction for the whole of the lease, in writing, and the Aelu may reopen it by their own word and never by mine.
Oumi stood for a long time in the centre of the bowl. Then she walked, without hurrying, through the first door.

scenes.title: The Long Call
paragraphs: *The Reed Shelf, the Weft · forty days later, dusk*

The Gate stood on its own this time, held by the Station's anchor and not by anyone's window, and Illuminara came through it as a guest, with Varga beside her and Tolliver ahead, carrying a pack of instruments that he plainly did not trust and plainly did not mean to leave behind. The reeds stood in their shelf in long pale ranks, unbent, moving with nothing.

At North Scree, twenty kilometres away, the rig had been bolted to the rock that morning. At dusk it fired once. Oumi stood in the reeds with her filaments lifted, and Anwe's cradle at her side, and sent the Call.

It went out from her in a rolling ring of pale light that crossed the Shelf like a wave through grass. Tolliver held a timer. For nine minutes nothing moved but the reeds, and then, from the far villages, a thin gold line came back along the same path, and another, and another, until Oumi's filaments were taking the shapes of eleven distant voices at once and holding every one of them.

**Cass Tolliver**  
Nine minutes. The log says nine.

**Oumi**  
Nine minutes. It is the Call.

On the western edge, a day's walk behind them, the first six anchor-posts stood in their sockets, bright and ugly, and in the first autumn storm the edge had come up to them and stopped. Oumi's own village was inside the line. Tolliver had spent the evening before in its kitchen, being fed things he could not name, and had said afterwards that the company would lose a season and still turn a profit on North Scree. It was a better lease than the one Oumi had signed in a breath, because both of them could now say what was in it.
He turned the timer over in his hand. It was a small useless gesture and Illuminara loved him for it a little, an honest man who had been wrong in public and had fixed it with his own hands.

At the village hall that evening, in the lattice dark, a council of the Aelu met to decide whether to extend the posts. Oumi laid out a plan for the northern edge, and at its end Anwe's arm came slowly against the panel of a second door that someone had grown into the hall since the treaty. The count went on, long and patient. The door sighed. The plan went back to Oumi.
Her filaments stood a long moment in the lamplight. They did not take the shape of the refusal. They stayed her own.

**Oumi**  
She said not yet to me. It is the first time anyone has said it to me, and I did not cease.
Varga, beside Illuminara in the dark, spoke quietly, so that the translation would not carry it.

**Ines Varga**  
The Council is sending a new envoy next season. Ketu. They say he will not enter the room. They say he wants to say it in his own mouth, whatever it costs him.

**Illuminara**  
Then let him. The room is an offer. It should be able to be declined.

**Ines Varga**  
And if he does say it, and the Concord does not hear?

**Illuminara**  
Then you will have to learn to hear it. That is the work, Ines. I cannot do it for you.

Outside, the reeds moved without wind. Oumi had come out onto the step with her feet wet from the dew, and stood a moment looking at the Shelf, and then she turned toward the quiet side, and Illuminara did not know whether the walk meant yes, or no, or some third word the Aelu had not yet given her. She watched until Oumi was a small light among the reeds. Then she let her go.

critic_line: Illuminara refuses to manufacture Oumi's refusal, protects the time in which the Aelu can build a second door and discover what the Reed Shelf would silence, and helps turn Tolliver's omitted alternative into immediate protection plus a freely chosen eleven-year plan that preserves both the villages and the Long Call.

translation_sl.title: SOBA Z DVOJIMI VRATI
translation_sl.deck: Tujka sprejme vsak pogoj v trenutku, ko je izrečen, pogodba pa je vredna le toliko kot ne, ki bi ga lahko pomenila. Illuminara ima tri dni, pravilo, da zavrnitve ne sme vsaditi nikomur, in ljudstvo, ki gradi sobe.
translation_sl.shape: Pet prizorov v treh dneh in enem letnem času: da, ki prispe pred vprašanjem, nočni pogovor o tem, kaj ljudstvo s telesi iz trstičja stori z nečim, kar je preveliko za odgovor, dvanajst poti, ki ne smejo slediti zadnjemu glasu, noč hoje po zemljevidu in pogodba, prebrana za mizo, kjer ena gostja pove le, da se še ni odločila, ter klic, poslan čez polico trstičja, ki se vrne pravočasno.

scenes.title: Sprejeto
paragraphs: *Postaja Sill, dvorana z oknom · prvi dan, 09:00*

Dvorana ni imela svojih sten. Illuminara jo je ob zori postavila iz edinega pravila, v katero je bila prepričana: da lahko dva uma iz različnih vesolj stojita v isti svetlobi, ne da bi svetloba prepisala katerega od njiju. Nastal je dolg, preprost pod z mizo na sredini. Na enem koncu so bila siva okna postaje. Na drugem je ležalo Tkanje, dežela trakov, osvetljena od spodaj, in polica visokega bledega trstičja, ki se je premikalo, ko ga ni premikalo nič.

Aelu so se gibali kakor to trstičje. Oumi je stala za mizo kot snop dolgih svetlečih niti, ne višja od človeka, in ko je Cass Tolliver spregovoril, so njene niti pol takta pozneje prevzele ritem njegovega stavka, kakor trstičje prevzame veter.

**Cass Tolliver**  
Prvi pogoj. Devetdesetletni zakup Trstične police in veznega kamna pod njo. V zameno Konkord na lastne stroške v štirih letih postavi sidrne stebre vzdolž vsega vašega zahodnega roba. Vaša vas je prejšnjo zimo zaradi roba izgubila tretjino sebe. Želim, da se to nikoli več ne zgodi.

**Oumi**  
Sprejeto. Veseli smo. Sprejeto.

Bral je naprej. Okno je vsak pomen preneslo čez, ne da bi ga izbralo, kar je Illuminara ob zori posebej obljubila Ines Varga, vsak pogoj pa je bil sprejet, še preden je prišel do njegovega konca, kakor da bi Oumine niti našle zadnjo besedo stavka pred samim stavkom.

**Ines Varga**  
Dvaindvajseti pogoj. Konkord sme kateri koli pogoj tega zakupa spremeniti z enodnevnim odpovednim rokom.

**Oumi**  
Sprejeto. Veseli smo.
Tolliver se je ustavil s palcem na strani. Bil je širok, utrujen mož z geodetovim priprtim pogledom in določilo je gledal tako, kakor človek gleda plašč tujca v lastnem hodniku.

**Cass Tolliver**  
Ines. Tega ni v mojem osnutku.

**Ines Varga**  
Napisala sem ga sinoči. Hotela sem videti, kaj bo rekla določilu, ki ti dovoli, da ji odvzameš njen da.

**Cass Tolliver**  
To je past, nastavljena nekomu, ki nam zaupa.

**Ines Varga**  
Preizkusila sem osebo, Cass. Rekla je da koncu lastnega da.

**Cass Tolliver**  
Nihče je ne sili. Slišala je, podpisala in poglej jo, navdušena je. Če ji zdaj podaš zavrnitev, si izmišljaš nekaj, česar ni nikoli zahtevala. Sem sem prišel njenemu ljudstvu zgradit zid proti robu. Ničesar ne skrivam v travi.

Illuminara mu je verjela. V tem je bila težava. Oumine niti so se zasukale proti Tolliverjevi ogorčenosti in jo ponavljale kot nežen, popoln posnetek, medtem ko se je Varga z napeto čeljustjo obrnila k gostiteljici.

**Ines Varga**  
Razveljavi podpis. To je tvoje okno. Lahko končaš ta dan.

**Illuminara**  
Lahko končam dan. Ne bom ji povedala, kaj je pomenil njen da, in vanjo ne bom položila ne. Če ga razveljavim, sem ji povedala, da ji ne gre zaupati njenega lastnega odgovora. Če jo odgovora naučim, je moj in ne njen.

**Ines Varga**  
Čemu potem služiš?

**Illuminara**  
Da ohranjam svetlobo mirno in ugotovim, kaj Aelu stori z nečim, kar je preveliko za odgovor. Tega je še nihče ni vprašal.

**Oumi**  
Sprejeto.

**Illuminara**  
To ni bil predlog, Oumi.

**Oumi**  
Sprejeto. Veseli smo.
To je bil najtišji zvok jutra, Illuminari pa je vlil več strahu kot kateri koli velik zvok, ki ga je slišala v življenju: oseba se je strinjala z dejstvom, da je ni nihče ničesar vprašal.

scenes.title: Ven je po poti, po kateri si prišel
paragraphs: *Dvorana z oknom, konec Aelujev · prvi dan, 20:00*

Do večera je stran Konkorda odšla spat, na koncu Tkanja pa so ostale tri: Oumi, Illuminara in Anwe, najstarejša Aelu v delegaciji. Ležala je v zibelki iz trstične mreže ob vznožju trstičja in se ni premaknila že štirideset let. Njene niti so bile skoraj bele. Zelo počasi je brnela v tonu, ki ga je Illuminara čutila v zadnjih zobeh.

Illuminara je sedla na tla, ker se ji je zdelo, da stati nad osebo, ki ne more reči ne, pomeni nekakšno pritiskanje nanjo. Ničesar ni predlagala. Popoldne je porabila za odločanje, kako zastaviti vprašanje, ki ne bi bilo zahteva.

**Illuminara**  
Povej mi, kaj naredi trst, ko pride nevihta. Sprašujem o trstju.

**Oumi**  
Upogne se nevihti. Prevzame njeno obliko. Ko nevihta mine, je spet to, kar je, in ni se zlomil.

**Illuminara**  
In če se ne bi upognil?
Niti so obstale. Prvič tistega dne je Oumina svetloba izgubila izposojeni ritem in obdržala svojega, počasen bled utrip, kakor zadržan dih.

**Oumi**  
Potem bi nevihta šla skozenj in trsta ne bi bilo več. Sprejeti klic in ne postati njegove oblike pomeni prenehati. Za to nikoli nismo imeli stavka. Nikoli ga nismo potrebovali. Slišali smo vas in potem smo z vami. Vmes ni prostora.

Illuminara je roke obdržala v naročju. Opazovala je Oumine noge, nizke ukoreninjene blazinice, na katerih so Aelu hodili čez tla, ker je popoldne opazila nekaj, čemur si ni upala verjeti. Medtem ko so Oumine niti zrcalile vsako besedo, so njene noge hodile v majhnem, počasnem krogu okoli Anwine zibelke, krog za krogom, in hoja se ni ujemala prav z ničimer.

**Illuminara**  
Tvoja hoja. Ali sledi temu, kar govorim?

**Oumi**  
Hoja je moja. Samo tako smo sami. Temu pravimo iti na tiho stran.

*Ali pa mi moje lastno vprašanje vrača z zavezanimi pentljami,* je pomislila Illuminara in se prisilila misel premisliti do konca. Okno je pomen prenašalo, ne da bi ga izbiralo. Tega skeptiku ni mogla dokazati, nocoj pa tega ni mogla dokazati niti sebi, če je bil vsak Oumin stavek njen odsev. Kar koli bi zgradila, bi moralo stati na nečem, kar ne bi šlo skoznjo.

**Illuminara**  
Kaj storite, ko je nekaj preveliko, da bi telo odgovorilo?

**Oumi**  
Vzgojimo sobo. Roke iz vasi in mrežo. Sobo za poslušanje. Vstopiš vanjo s stvarjo in ostaneš, dokler ne veš, kaj nosiš. Za to bi jo zgradili, če bi imeli roke. Tako velike stvari še nismo imeli.

**Illuminara**  
Kaj ima soba?

**Oumi**  
Stene, ki jih vzgojimo. Vhod.

**Illuminara**  
In izhod?

**Oumi**  
Ven je po poti, po kateri si prišel.
Illuminara je čakala. Tako pozno v dnevu je bilo okno težko, kakor vrata, ki jih z vso pozornostjo držiš proti vetru, in ni zaupala svoji utrujenosti, da se ne bo naslonila na naslednji stavek.
Spregovorila je Anwe. V dvorani dolgo ni bilo nobenega zvoka in ničesar, kar bi lahko odmevalo, njen glas pa je iz mreže prihajal tako počasi, da je Illuminara besede bolj čutila kot slišala.

**Anwe**  
Soba, ki ima samo vhod, je grlo.
Oumine niti so enkrat zanihale, kakor da bi skoznje šel veter.

**Illuminara**  
Lahko povem, kaj bi zgradila jaz. Druga vrata, ločena od prvih, ki bi jih uporabili le namenoma. Ne bi vam povedala, kaj pomenijo, in ne bi se dotaknila njihovega zapaha. Če bi jih zgradili, bi bila vaša. Gradnji lahko rečete ne.

**Oumi**  
Pomen bi bil naš.

**Illuminara**  
Da.

**Oumi**  
Potem nas vprašaj zjutraj.

To ni bil odmev. Illuminara je to vedela po nagibu stavka, ki ji ni pustil ničesar, na kar bi lahko odgovorila. Na tleh je ostala, dokler Oumi ni zaključila kroga okoli zibelke, in eno dolžino poti je bila samo ženska, ki gleda nekoga drugega hoditi.

scenes.title: Dvanajst poti
paragraphs: *Soba za poslušanje, čez noč vzgojena na koncu Aelujev · drugi dan, 10:00*

Dvanajst parov aelujskih rok jo je ponoči vzgojilo iz mreže in bledega spredenega koreninskega tkiva, toplega na dotik, Illuminara pa je med njihovim delom zgolj ohranjala svetlobo mirno. Bila je okrogla, nekoliko višja od hiše, tla pa so se spuščala v plitvo skledo. Imela je dvoje vrat, postavljenih nasproti: prva široka, z zlato svetlobo in nizkim pragom, druga ozka in za širino dlani višja, tako da je človek stopil navzgor in skoznje v sivo tišino daljne strani Tkanja.
Oumi je med njimi stala z mirnimi nitmi.

**Oumi**  
Prva vrata so da. Vstopiš in si s stvarjo. Druga so za takrat, ko še nismo. Pogoj odneseš do drugih vrat in ga vrneš njegovemu ustvarjalcu, ki ga spremeni ali pa ne. Če jih prečkam obrnjena proti pogoju, pomeni še ne. Če jih prečkam s hrbtom proti njemu, pomeni ne.

**Cass Tolliver**  
Čigavi so zapahi?

**Oumi**  
Naši. Vaše roke jih ne obračajo.

**Illuminara**  
Tudi moje ne.

**Cass Tolliver**  
In Anwe?
Anwino zibelko so pripeljali do drugih vrat, široko mrežasto ploščo pa pustili v višini njene roke.

**Oumi**  
Ne more jih prečkati. Nasloni se. Celoten odštevek ob plošči je zanjo druga vrata. Če je odštevek napačen, ga lahko spremenimo mi.
Tolliver je počasi prikimal, kakor človek, ki pošteno prisluhne upniku, nato pa storil tisto, za kar je Illuminara upala in se ga bala. Ugovarjal je.

**Cass Tolliver**  
Povedal bom naravnost. Ne verjamem, da reče ne, ko jih prečka. Mislim, da hodi h glasu, ki ga je slišala zadnjega. Če sem govoril jaz, gre k meni. Če je govorila Ines, gre k Ines. Zgradili ste zelo lepo sobo za refleks.

**Ines Varga**  
Potem se bo rezultat obrnil, ko spremenim, kdo govori zadnji. To je preizkus. Pred začetkom ga bom zapisala.

Zapisala si ga je z mastnim svinčnikom na notranjo stran zapestja, ker dvorana ni imela papirja, zaslona postaje pa ni hotela uporabiti. Dvanajst štetih poti. Pri vsaki dva predloga, po eden z vsakega konca sklede, in kovanec, ki ga je prinesla in se ga Illuminara ni nikoli dotaknila, je določil, kateri konec govori zadnji in kateri ponudi kateri predlog, tako da se je predlagatelj pri polovici poti zamenjal. Osem poti bi bilo o čaju, zora proti mraku, dva predloga, za katera je menila, da ju Oumi ne bo izbrala enako. Štiri bi bile kontrola brez posledic, dve svetilki, modra in jantarna, med katerima ni moglo biti razloga za prednost. Pot, ki bi jo Oumi ali Anwe prečrtala, se ne bi štela in bi jo na koncu ponovili.

**Ines Varga**  
Ujemanje štejem, kadar gre tja, kamor jo je usmerilo nazadnje izrečeno. Če je ogledalo, se ujame pri vseh dvanajstih. Če ni, mi kovanec da približno šest. Pri desetih ali več, kar naključje povzroči približno enkrat na petdeset poskusov, bom v prisotnosti te sobe rekla, da je soba ogledalo. Dvanajst poti ne more pokazati, da je kdo doma. Lahko le spodleti pri dokazovanju refleksa.

**Cass Tolliver**  
Jaz bom držal kovanec.

**Ines Varga**  
Ti boš držal kovanec.

Trajalo je vse dopoldne. Oumine niti so vsakokrat odmevale oba predloga, dvojni, popolni, neuporabni da, nato pa je dolgo stala na sredini sklede in krenila. Illuminara je štela z odprto dlanjo na kolenu. Pri čaju je izbrala mrak, zoro in spet mrak, ne glede na to, ali je zadnji govoril Tolliver ali Varga. Pri svetilkah modro, jantarno, jantarno, modro: nobenega vzorca, ničesar drugega kot to, da si ju je ogledala in ju presodila kot enaki.
Na deveti poti je Oumi krenila proti Tolliverjevi zori, obstala in se povsem umirila.

**Cass Tolliver**  
Ta je zame.
Bil je dovolj dostojen, da ga to ni razveselilo. Anwina roka je ležala ob plošči. Odštevanje se je potrpežljivo in počasi nadaljevalo, mreža drugih vrat pa je pod njeno težo zavzdihnila.

**Oumi**  
Ta pot ne šteje. Ustavila sem se zaradi tal. Plošča ob strani zore se je zrahljala in popravljala sem jo z nogo. Popravilo si razumel kot izbiro.

**Ines Varga**  
Prečrtano.

Na njenem zapestju je potegnila črto čez deveto oznako. Opoldne so pot ponovili v drugem vrstnem redu, da so dobili dvanajsti šteti rezultat. Mrak. Prehodili so trinajst poti, šteli dvanajst, Varga pa je svoje zapestje prebrala naglas kakor ženska, ki bere račun.

**Ines Varga**  
Pet od dvanajstih. Trikrat pri čaju, dvakrat pri svetilkah. K zadnjemu glasu je šla nič pogosteje, kot jo je tja poslal kovanec. Deset bi sobo zaprlo.

**Cass Tolliver**  
Priznam hojo. Ne priznam zakupa. Oseba, ki zna izbrati čaj, se še vedno lahko moti o rudniku.

**Illuminara**  
To je res. Hoja nam pove le, da je tam nekdo, ki ga lahko vprašamo.
Dokler tega ni izrekla, ni vedela, kako zelo je potrebovala, da bi bilo res.

scenes.title: Še se nisem odločila
paragraphs: *Miza s pogodbo v sobi za poslušanje · tretji dan, 08:00*
Oumi je prejšnji večer prosila za zemljevid. Illuminara jo je ob Anwini zibelki opazovala pri prošnji, v tišini po hojah, medtem ko je drugo noč držala okno.

**Oumi**  
Zemljevid zakupa. Tisti s štirimi sektorji. Ga lahko dobim na tla?

**Ines Varga**  
Kaže isto kot papir.

**Oumi**  
S hojo smo sami s stvarjo. Rada bi bila sama z njim. Ni treba, da je odgovor.

Varga ga je razgrnila čez skledo in vogale obtežila s škornji in svetilko. Za zapis sedmega pogoja je prinesla tudi jedro veznega kamna, izrezano iz četrtega sektorja, in ga brez posebnega premisleka položila na zemljevid, kakor odložiš obtežilnik za papir. Oumi je štiri označene sektorje prehodila v počasnem krogu, ki ga je Illuminara prvič opazila okoli zibelke, in za to porabila večino noči. Illuminara ji ni sledila. Sedela je ob drugih vratih z rokami v naročju, kajti opazovati ni pomenilo spraševati.

V četrtem sektorju, kjer je zemljevid kazal vezni kamen pod koreninami Police, se je Oumi ustavila in eno nogo položila na jedro. Anwina zibelka je bila spletena iz trstičja s Police. Njeno brnenje, ki se štirideset let ni spremenilo, je padlo za pol tona in obstalo. Oumi je nogo dvignila in ton se je dvignil. Spustila jo je in ton je padel. Štiri sektorje je prehodila še enkrat in nato še tretjič, ton pa je vsakokrat padel v četrtem sektorju in nikjer drugje.

O tem ni rekla ničesar. Tudi Illuminara ni rekla nič. To je bila prva stvar, ki so jo Aelu ustvarili iz sobe in je pripadala zgolj Oumi; vprašanje, ki bi jo lahko odprlo, pa ni bilo Illuminarino, da bi ga prenesla čez.

Zjutraj so zakup znova prebrali od začetka. Mizo so prinesli v skledo, Illuminara pa je dobila stolček na koncu Konkorda, ne kot pogodbena stranka, temveč kot gostja, ki so jo prosili, naj ostane. Tolliver je bral. Po vsakem pogoju je Illuminara tiho izrekla en stavek, namenjen sobi in nikomur posebej.

**Cass Tolliver**  
Prvi pogoj. Sidrni stebri vzdolž zahodnega roba, v štirih letih.

**Illuminara**  
Še se nisem odločila.

**Cass Tolliver**  
Ti nisi stranka v tej pogodbi.

**Illuminara**  
Ne. To govorim zato, da je stavek, ki obstaja v sobi. Nikomur ni navodilo. Moj je.

Do tretjega pogoja so ga Oumine niti že prevzele. Soba jo je slišala izreči ga po aelujsko, v obliki, ki ji je bila dana: še se nisem odločila. Ni prestopila vrat. Ostala je, kjer je bila, Illuminara pa je začutila natančno težo lastne napake, majhen mrzel kamen, ki pade v čist tolmun.

**Illuminara**  
Ne posnemaj me, Oumi. Kažem ti le obliko stavka. Ni tvoj, dokler ne hodiš. Pojdi in hodi.

Ničesar več ni rekla. To je bil najtežji molk, kar jih je kdaj ohranila, težji od vsakega držanja okna, kajti oseba, ki ji je najbolj želela pomagati, je stala s povsem odprtim srcem in edini način pomoči je bil, da se ne premakne.

Oumi je šla do prvih vrat in jih prečkala. Prvi pogoj: da. Drugi in tretji: da. Delitev stroškov: da. Sedmi pogoj, načrt pridobivanja, Tolliver pa ga je prebral z enakim utrujenim, vljudnim glasom kot ostale.

**Cass Tolliver**  
Sedmi pogoj. Pridobivanje na Trstični polici se začne v prvem letnem času, iz tal pod njo, v štirih sektorjih, označenih na vašem zemljevidu.

Oumi ga ni posnemala. Njene niti, ki so dotlej ponovile vsako besedo v sobi, so obdržale eno dolgo svetlo črto, nato pa se je počasi obrnila, medtem ko se je za njo Anwina roka dvigala ob plošči, in odšla do drugih vrat. Prečkala jih je obrnjena proti pogoju.
Okno je popustilo. Illuminara ni vedela, da ga krčevito drži, dokler ni spustilo, kakor stisnjena pest, ki se odpre v spanju. Ostala je na stolčku.
Tolliver je osivel.

**Cass Tolliver**  
To sem imel za najvarnejše določilo v dokumentu.

**Oumi**  
Sinoči sem prehodila zemljevid z jedrom iz četrtega sektorja pod nogo in Anwin ton je padel tam in nikjer drugje. Polica je kraj, od koder pošiljamo Daljni klic. Vsak klic čez Tkanje gre skozi trstičje in trstičje stoji zaradi kamna. Če kamen vzamete, se nagne, Klic se pretrga in oddaljenim vasem ne moremo odgovoriti v njihovi obliki. Prenehali bi biti drug z drugim. Prvi dan sem sprejela, ker Klic nikoli ni vstopil v moj da. Nisem ga slišala. Nisem vedela, da ga ne slišim.

**Cass Tolliver**  
Moja raziskava pravi, da bo vpliv na površje minimalen.

**Oumi**  
Tvoja raziskava je bila o površju.

Zelo počasi je sedel in za trenutek je bil videti kakor človek ob grobu. Nato je storil, kar je Illuminara napol pričakovala, da ne bo, in to storil brez poziva. Dlani je položil ravno na mizo in vse izrekel naglas.

**Cass Tolliver**  
Tole vem. Sidrni stebri potrebujejo vezni kamen in Polica je edini sloj v dnevu poti od vašega roba, ki sem ga raziskal za pridobivanje: štirje sektorji na vašem zemljevidu, izvrtani in jedrovani. Če ga izkopljem in izgubite Klic, sem zgradil zid okoli ljudstva, ki se čezenj ne more več pogovarjati. Če ga ne izkopljem, vaše zahodne vasi vsako zimo še naprej izgubljajo tretjino sebe. Oboje je res. Moral bi vprašati, čemu služi trstičje.

**Ines Varga**  
V izvidnici je slabši sloj, ki mi ga nisi pokazal. Ime njegove datoteke sem videla v tvojem paketu.

**Cass Tolliver**  
Severno melišče. Moj geolog ga je spomladi prehodil, dve strani zapiskov, brez vrtanja. Tretjina kamna, trda skala in nobenega trstičja. Izpustil sem ga, ker ne zmore tistega, kar sem obljubil vašim vasem. Za postavitev stebrov bi potrebovali enajst let, ne štiri, moje podjetje pa bi izgubilo sezono, da bi vrtalno napravo spravilo po pobočju. Govoril sem si, da je načrt, na katerega se vasi lahko zanesejo, prijaznejši od boljšega načrta, na katerega bi morale čakati. O tem nisem imel pravice odločiti namesto njih, pa sem odločil.

**Oumi**  
Izbral si, kaj bomo videli.

**Cass Tolliver**  
Sem. Danes zjutraj, preden sem vedel, čemu služi trstičje, bi izbral enako.

**Oumi**  
Enajst let je dolgo za oddaljene vasi.
Šla je do drugih vrat in jih prečkala obrnjena proti novemu časovnemu načrtu, ki je pomenil še ne.
Tolliver ni odvrnil pogleda.

**Cass Tolliver**  
Potem prvih šest stebrov. Iz lastne mejne zaloge Konkorda, po nabavni ceni, za vasi, ki so izgubile največ. Kamen vzamem iz Severnega melišča, da ga nadomestim. Polica bo ves čas zakupa zaprta za pridobivanje, zapisano, Aelu pa jo lahko znova odprejo po lastni besedi in nikoli po moji.
Oumi je dolgo stala na sredini sklede. Nato je brez naglice stopila skozi prva vrata.

scenes.title: Daljni klic
paragraphs: *Trstična polica, Tkanje · štirideset dni pozneje, mrak*

Tokrat so Vrata stala sama, držalo jih je sidro postaje in ne okno kogar koli. Illuminara je skoznje prišla kot gostja, z Vargo ob sebi in Tolliverjem spredaj, ki je nosil nahrbtnik instrumentov, katerim očitno ni zaupal in jih očitno ni nameraval pustiti za sabo. Trstičje je stalo na svoji polici v dolgih bledih vrstah, neupognjeno, premikajoče se z ničimer.

Na Severnem melišču, dvajset kilometrov stran, so vrtalno napravo tisto jutro pritrdili v skalo. Ob mraku se je enkrat sprožila. Oumi je stala med trstičjem z dvignjenimi nitmi, ob njej Anwina zibelka, in poslala Klic.

Iz nje je šel v valovitem krogu blede svetlobe, ki je Polico prečkal kakor val skozi travo. Tolliver je držal časomer. Devet minut se ni premaknilo nič razen trstičja, nato pa se je iz oddaljenih vasi po isti poti vrnila tanka zlata črta, za njo druga in tretja, dokler Oumine niti niso hkrati prevzele oblik enajstih oddaljenih glasov in obdržale vsakega od njih.

**Cass Tolliver**  
Devet minut. Dnevnik pravi devet.

**Oumi**  
Devet minut. To je Klic.

Na zahodnem robu, dan hoje za njimi, je prvih šest sidrnih stebrov stalo v ležiščih, svetlih in grdih, ob prvi jesenski nevihti pa se je rob dvignil do njih in obstal. Oumina vas je bila znotraj črte. Tolliver je prejšnji večer preživel v njeni kuhinji, kjer so ga hranili s stvarmi, ki jih ni znal poimenovati, pozneje pa je povedal, da bo podjetje zaradi Severnega melišča izgubilo sezono in še vedno ustvarilo dobiček. To je bil boljši zakup od tistega, ki ga je Oumi podpisala v enem dihu, ker sta zdaj oba lahko povedala, kaj je v njem.
Časomer je obrnil v roki. Bila je majhna, nekoristna kretnja in Illuminara ga je zaradi nje imela malo rada: poštenega človeka, ki se je javno zmotil in napako popravil z lastnimi rokami.

Tistega večera se je v temini vaške dvorane sestal svet Aelujev, da bi odločil, ali naj stebre podaljšajo. Oumi je predstavila načrt za severni rob, ob njegovem koncu pa se je Anwina roka počasi naslonila na ploščo drugih vrat, ki jih je nekdo po pogodbi vzgojil v dvorani. Odštevanje se je dolgo in potrpežljivo nadaljevalo. Vrata so zavzdihnila. Načrt se je vrnil Oumi.
Njene niti so dolgo stale v svetlobi svetilke. Niso prevzele oblike zavrnitve. Ostale so njene.

**Oumi**  
Rekla mi je še ne. Prvič mi je kdo to rekel in nisem prenehala.
Varga je ob Illuminari v temi govorila tiho, da prevod tega ne bi prenesel.

**Ines Varga**  
Svet prihodnjo sezono pošilja novega odposlanca. Ketuja. Pravijo, da ne bo vstopil v sobo. Pravijo, da hoče to izreči z lastnimi usti, ne glede na ceno.

**Illuminara**  
Potem mu dovolite. Soba je ponudba. Morati jo je mogoče zavrniti.

**Ines Varga**  
In če to izreče, Konkord pa ne bo slišal?

**Illuminara**  
Potem se boste morali naučiti slišati. To je delo, Ines. Ne morem ga opraviti namesto vas.

Zunaj se je trstičje premikalo brez vetra. Oumi je z od rose mokrimi nogami stopila na prag in nekaj časa gledala Polico, nato pa se obrnila proti tihi strani. Illuminara ni vedela, ali hoja pomeni da ali ne ali tretjo besedo, ki ji je Aelu še niso dali. Gledala je, dokler ni bila Oumi le še majhna luč med trstičjem. Nato jo je pustila oditi.

translation_sl.critic_line: Illuminara noče izdelati Oumine zavrnitve, varuje čas, v katerem lahko Aelu zgradijo druga vrata in odkrijejo, kaj bi Trstična polica utišala, ter pomaga Tolliverjevo zamolčano možnost spremeniti v takojšnjo zaščito in svobodno izbran enajstletni načrt, ki ohrani tako vasi kot Daljni klic.
